This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 06.11.2023 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Raichur in MVC No.308/2022.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 29.03.2022, deceased Udaykumar was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-36/EW-3870 on Gangavathi-Sindhanur main road, infront of ESSAR petrol Bunk, at that time respondent No.1 rider of scooty bearing Reg.No.KA-36/ER-7697 came in a rash and negligent manner suddenly turned wrong NC: 2025:KHC-K:7522-DB HC-KAR side and dashed to the deceased motorcycle, at that time, respondent No.3 driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 36/F-370 came from Gangavathi side in a rash and negligent manner with high speed run away on the deceased Udaykumar due to which, he died on the spot.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.

4. Upon service of notice, the respondents appeared through their counsel and respondent Nos.2 and 4 have filed their separate written statements wherein respondent No.3 adopted the written statement of respondent No.4 denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim Pallavi And Ors vs B Satyanarayana And Ors on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192738991/
3 petition and held that NC: 2025:KHC-K:7522-DB HC-KAR the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.32,44,900/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 being insurer of respondent No.1 scooty vehicle and respondent No.4 being self insurer of KSRTC bus are directed to deposit the compensation amount to the extent of 80% (to be payable by respondent No.2) and 20% (to be payable by respondent No.4) along with interest.

sentences.text:
Being aggrieved,
the present appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimants assert that the deceased was aged about 22 years at the time of the accident and had a monthly income of Rs.30,000-/ to Rs.35,000/- by working as clerk at Veerabhadreshwara Trading company, Sindhanur, APMC.
However, the assessment of monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,250/- by the Tribunal is unjustified and erroneous.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7522-DB HC-KAR b)
Secondly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and on the lower side.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:
a) Firstly, although the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- to Rs.35,000/- per month, they have failed to substantiate their claim with supporting documents.
Consequently, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased notionally.
b) Secondly, on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
With the above NC: 2025:KHC-K:7522-DB HC-KAR contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that deceased Udaykumar died in the road traffic accident occurred on 29.03.2022 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

10. The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.30,000 to Rs.35,000/- per month by working as Clerk in APMC, Sindhanur Veerabhadreshwara Trading Company, but failed to produce supporting documents to substantiate their claim.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has rightly considered notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,250/- and rightly added future prospects and applied the correct multiplier.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal NC: 2025:KHC-K:7522-DB HC-KAR under the head of 'loss of dependency' is just and reasonable.

Even the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of loss of estate,
funeral expenses and loss of consortium is also just and reasonable.
Hence, we find that the appeal is devoid of merit and is liable to be dismissed.

12. In the result we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is dismissed confirming the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
Sd/-
